claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start by beginning the eligibility assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To start with, I need to understand the children you're claiming for.

**How old is your child (or your youngest child if you have more than one)?**

The age of your child is important because it determines the path we need to follow:

- **Under 16 years old** - Children under 16 automatically qualify in most circumstances
- **16 to 19 years old** - We need to check if they're in education or training
- **20 years or older** - Unfortunately, they wouldn't qualify for Child Benefit

Could you tell me:
1. The age(s) of your child/children?
2. How many children are you inquiring about?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! I'm inquiring about my daughter Alex. She's 8 years old, so just the one child.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Thank you for that information. So I'm assessing eligibility for your daughter **Alex, who is 8 years old**.

Since Alex is under 16, let me navigate to the next step in the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week, or is she not in paid work at all?**

Since Alex is only 8 years old, I'd expect this would be a "yes" (she's not working), but I need to confirm this for the assessment.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, she's not working at all. She's only 8, so she's just at school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's exactly what I'd expect for an 8-year-old. Let me move forward with the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Is Alex NOT receiving any of these benefits in her own right:**
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA)
- Universal Credit

For an 8-year-old, this would typically be "yes" (she's not receiving these), but I need to confirm this for the assessment.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: That's right, she doesn't receive any benefits in her own name.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Is Alex in an apprenticeship?**

At 8 years old, this would almost certainly be "no", but I need to confirm:
- Is Alex NOT in any form of apprenticeship?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, she's not in an apprenticeship. She's only 8, so she's just in primary school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That makes sense. Let me continue to the next stage of the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check the **residency requirements**. This is an important part of the assessment.

Can you tell me:

**Do you normally live in the UK?**

The main paths that would qualify are:
- You normally live in the UK
- You have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme
- You have pre-settled status and meet certain conditions (working, studying, seeking work, etc.)
- You're a Crown servant living abroad in certain qualifying countries

Which of these applies to you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK. I'm in Manchester.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! That's clear. Let me continue to the next stage of the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to check **your responsibility for Alex**.

Can you confirm:

**Do you live with Alex and are you responsible for her care?**

For context, responsibility means either:
- You live with the child, OR
- You contribute to their upkeep (food, clothes, housing, pocket money, etc.), OR
- You're paying maintenance under a court order or agreement

For your 8-year-old daughter in your household, I'd expect this would be "yes", but I need to confirm.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives with me at home and I take care of her.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Is there anyone else claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or has anyone else applied for Child Benefit for her?**

This is an important question because only one person can claim Child Benefit for each child. So:
- Is there no other claimant for Alex?
- OR is there another person claiming/has applied, but you've agreed who should claim?
- OR is there a dispute about who should claim?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for her. It's just me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Where is Alex living at the moment?**

- Is she living at home with you normally?
- OR is she currently in hospital?
- OR is she in care?
- OR is she in a fostering arrangement?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: She's living at home with me normally.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Let me continue to the next stage.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Almost there! Just one final question:

**Is the local council NOT paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

In other words, you're paying for her care yourself and the council isn't supporting her financially?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: That's right, I'm paying for everything myself. The council isn't giving me any money for her care.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! That's the final piece of information I need. Let me now provide you with the eligibility outcome.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Now let me record your eligibility outcome:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## ✅ **You Are ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit**

Congratulations! You meet all the eligibility requirements to claim Child Benefit for your daughter **Alex**.

### **Summary of Your Eligibility:**

✓ Alex is 8 years old (under 16)
✓ She's not working
✓ She's not receiving ESA or Universal Credit
✓ She's not in an apprenticeship
✓ You live in the UK (Manchester)
✓ Alex lives with you and you are responsible for her care
✓ No one else is claiming for her
✓ The council is not paying towards her care

---

### **Next Steps - How to Claim:**

1. **Apply online** at www.gov.uk/child-benefit or **by post** using form CH2
2. **Provide documents:**
   - Proof of your identity
   - Alex's birth certificate or adoption certificate
   - Proof of your address

3. **Important note about High Income Child Benefit Charge:**
   - If you or a partner earn over £60,000 per year, you may have to repay some or all of the Child Benefit through Self Assessment tax returns, even though you still qualify

4. **Payment frequency:**
   - Usually paid every 4 weeks
   - If you're a single parent or receiving certain benefits, you can ask for weekly payments

For more information, visit: https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?

All eligibility criteria are met.
